answer: Divergent thread binding: each identity must keep a continuous, hash-chained interaction thread whose state root references a random walnut challenge from the prior epoch. Verification requires revealing the preimage that advances only that identity's chain. A clone farm copying one thread hits a fork at the challenge point; since clones cannot diverge into distinct valid histories without each paying an independent registration and per-epoch challenge-solving cost, the attacker pays full per-identity compute plus a harbor deposit forfeited on any fork detection.
